Nothing is committed (HEAD is still 34b721c). Treat that work as a starting point to read, check and finish, not as done and not as something to redo from scratch: the scout reports what the tree holds against this brief (git status, git diff, and each new file), the builder keeps what is right, completes what is missing and fixes what is wrong, and the tester, reviewer and recorder work on the finished tree as usual. The brief's line numbers were measured on the clean tree and may have moved. Also note: main has moved since this brief was written (fc8109d, Friday, October 23, puts Support back in the header's More menu, one line in src/components/layout/Navbar.tsx); the base for this slice stays 34b721c and the lead merges main into the branch after this slice's commit, so do not merge or rebase anything. A test that fails the day K turns a switch on is wrong, as the step 32 review ruled for the Checkpoint D switch test. (2) The reload guard lives in a small module of its own that src/main.tsx calls before createRoot, as the brief says; its unit test imports the module, and a second test reads src/main.tsx's text to pin the call. (3) If the 1.4 copy's sha256 or byte count below does not match the file, the lead has applied the final review's fixes to the copy since this brief was written: take the file as it is, and check only that its "- WS01:" bullet under "Deviations from v1.1" is byte for byte the 1.3 line (the sha256 of that line below still holds) and that the file has no em or en dash. WS02 slice 1 of 19 (ws02-01-record-checkpoint-d-and-open-ws02), the first slice of the information architecture and navigation workstream: the header, the tablet and phone bars, the footer, search, the personal event strip and the My LCA menu. WS02 is built on branch redesign/ws02-navigation, cut from main at 34b721c (the merge of pull request 108, WS01's checkpoint D), and merged in five checkpoints whose letters carry on from WS01's A to D: checkpoint E is slices 1 to 5, F is 6 to 8, G is 9 to 11, H is 12 to 16 and I is 17 to 19. Each checkpoint is a draft pull request against main, merged after a merge-safety review as WS01's were. This slice is the first of checkpoint E; the lead opens E's draft pull request after this slice's commit, so the pull request text this slice drafts is E's first description, which slices 2 to 5 extend. The branch HEAD is 34b721c (equal to origin/main), the working tree is clean when the slice starts, and the base for diffs is the commit in `base` (main's tip, 34b721c). The local ref `main` is stale (4c1a466, 717 files away from HEAD): never diff against it, and never use it to judge what this slice changed.

Precedence and where to read. In this brief <scratchpad> means the session's scratch folder, <scratchpad> (an environment directory: its name never goes into a record, a test, a commit text or a pull request text). The lead's notes win over the manifest and over this brief where they differ, and the standing rules and the gate in docs/redesign/HANDOFF.md still bind every slice: <scratchpad>/ws02-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 1) is in <scratchpad>/docs2-wt/docs/redesign/ws02-manifest.json (read slice 1, and the top-level sequencing_rationale, deviations_from_brief and open_questions_for_k); the plan notes are <scratchpad>/docs2-wt/docs/redesign/ws02-plan-notes.md (read 'Before step 1', 'How each step is built' and 'Review'); the handoff sheet is <scratchpad>/docs2-wt/docs/redesign/HANDOFF.md ('Standing rules' and 'How a slice is built'). None of those files is on this branch (they live on the documents branch and in the scratchpad), so read them at these paths. Brief 1.4 is <scratchpad>/brief14/REDESIGN_SPEC.1.4.md, with the untouched 1.3 copy beside it as REDESIGN_SPEC.before-1.4.md and the assembly notes (questions for K and their defaults) as assembly-notes.md. Where the manifest and the lead's notes disagree, the lead's notes are followed and the difference is recorded; the differences found while composing this brief are listed at the end under 'Where this brief departs from the manifest'.

What this slice is, in one view. It is records and tests plus two small changes to code the site is built from. In order: (1) brief 1.4 lands as docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md, copied whole; (2) every switch that 1.4's flag table names and src/lib/features.ts lacks is added, each false with a plain one-line comment, and the three tests that read the table follow; (3) a once-only reload on the build loader's 'vite:preloadError' event goes into src/main.tsx, with a unit test; (4) REDESIGN_STATUS.md records checkpoint D's merge, moves the date line, and opens WS02's section with its mapping, step block, decisions, deviations, verify items and follow-ups; (5) a record test of its own pins the new text; (6) the commit text and the pull request text are drafted. No page, style, server, migration, worker or build-config file changes. With every switch off a visitor sees nothing new, except that a browser tab left open across a deploy now recovers by itself. Nothing is added to package.json.

The stale tab. src/main.tsx today handles no 'vite:preloadError' event (grep over src and test finds none); the only recovery is the ErrorBoundary's 'Something went wrong' screen with a refresh button. The build loader (vite 8.1.5) dispatches the event on window when a lazy file or one of its preloads fails: node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js line 28194 to 28199 builds new Event('vite:preloadError', { cancelable: true }), sets e.payload to the error, calls window.dispatchEvent(e) and throws the error only when e.defaultPrevented is false (node_modules/vite/client.d.ts line 284 types it; the built preload helper in dist-a11y-on/assets carries the same code). If the handler prevents the default, the loader's promise resolves with undefined, so the lazy page's render can throw once and the boundary can flash for an instant while the reload begins; the record says so. What happened: on Thursday, October 22 K's admin tab of /governance/minutes, open since before the checkpoint D deploy, fell into the 'Something went wrong' screen on 'Add document': the tab's index named the editor's lazy file under its old content hash, which the new deployment no longer serves. A hard refresh fixed it. With a deploy per checkpoint from now on this recurs for any open tab. src/main.tsx imports and renders at once (createRoot at line 19), so a test cannot import it; the guard's logic therefore sits in a small module of its own that main.tsx imports and calls before createRoot, outside the `if (FEATURES.newLook)` block, and a second test reads main.tsx's source to pin that it calls it.

4. The stale-tab reload. Add a small module (suggested src/lib/reloadOnStaleChunk.ts, name it in the record) and call it from src/main.tsx before createRoot, not inside the newLook block. Behaviour: it adds a listener on window for 'vite:preloadError'. When the event arrives and a sessionStorage mark (a fixed key, such as 'lca-stale-reload', written with the time or '1') is not set: set the mark, call event.preventDefault(), and reload the page once (location.reload()). When the mark is already set: do nothing (do not prevent the default), so the error reaches the ErrorBoundary exactly as today and the page cannot loop. Reading or writing sessionStorage is wrapped in try and catch; if either throws (private windows, blocked storage), do nothing and let the error through, because the once-only rule cannot be kept. The mark is never cleared by the guard. The function takes its window, storage and reload as arguments (with the real ones as defaults) so a unit test can drive it with a plain event target, a fake storage and a spy, in node or with a jsdom comment at the top of the file as other tests do. No switch: it changes nothing a visitor sees except that a stale tab recovers on its own. The new unit test (suggested test/unit/reload-on-stale-chunk.test.ts) pins: a listener for exactly 'vite:preloadError' is added once; the first event is prevented, sets the mark and reloads once; a second event with the mark set is not prevented and does not reload; storage that throws on read, or on write, neither prevents nor reloads; the event name is the loader's own (check it also appears in the installed vite's source by reading node_modules/vite/client.d.ts); and main.tsx's source calls the function before createRoot and outside the newLook block. Keep client-sections-audit passing: the module imports nothing from contracts or zod. The record states the why in plain words (K's admin tab on Thursday, October 22; one deploy per checkpoint from now on), that the event name is the build loader's own, that no switch guards it, and the instant of the boundary described above.
